connect(device_index)[source]¶

Connect a device in the Spike software. For USB devices, provide the serial number of the device to connect. For networked devices, send a string with format SOCKET::IP::PORT (e.g., SOCKET::192.168.1.1::12345). Returns 0 or 1 depending on if the device successfully opened.

Parameters:

device_index (int or str) – The index (serial number) or connection string of the device to connect.

get_count()[source]¶

Returns the number of devices connected to the PC. Note: No device may be active when this function is called. You must call DISConnect? before calling this function. Any networked devices that have been configured will be counted in the returned value.

Returns:

The number of devices connected to the PC.

Return type:

int

get_current()[source]¶

Returns the currently active device’s connection string. See LIST? for format.

Returns:

The currently active device.

Return type:

str

get_list()[source]¶

Returns the connection strings for all devices available to connect in the Spike software. For USB devices, this is serial numbers returned as ASCII integers and comma separated. For networked devices, the format is SOCKET::IP::PORT (e.g., SOCKET::192.168.1.1::12345). Use the COUNt? function to determine how many devices are present.

Returns:

The list of connected devices.

Return type:

str

is_active()[source]¶

Returns whether or not a device is currently connected and active in the software. You can use the IDN? function to request information about the device.

Returns:

True if a device is currently connected and active, False otherwise.

Return type:

bool

is_disconnected()[source]¶

Disconnects any device actively connected in Spike.

Returns:

True if successfully disconnected, False otherwise.

Return type:

bool

close()[source]¶

Disconnect any active device and close the Spike software.

This command disconnects any active device and closes the Spike software. It also terminates the socket connection with the Spike software. Note: There is not a way to reopen the software using SCPI commands.

is_preset()[source]¶

Query if the active device is preset.

This command closes and reopens the active device. The process can take between 6-20 seconds depending on the device type. Returns 1 for success, 0 otherwise.

Returns:

True if system is preset, False otherwise.

Return type:

bool

load_user_preset(filename)[source]¶

Load a user preset from the given file name.

If the preset does not exist, nothing occurs. The file name should have extension “.ini”.

Parameters:

filename (str) – The file name to load the preset. Should have extension “.ini”.

preset()[source]¶

Preset the active device.

This command power cycles the active device and returns the software to the initial power-on state. The process can take between 6-20 seconds depending on the device type.
